sources.entry: CSV Quick Look - Quick Look extension for CSV and TSV files with virtual scrolling, sorting, filtering, and dark mode. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/adamorad/csv-quick-look) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS Quick Look extension that replaces the plain-text preview of CSV and TSV files with a spreadsheet-style table.
summary.what_it_does: Press Space on a .csv or .tsv file in Finder to get a table preview. The table uses virtual scrolling so only visible rows are in the DOM, and the README says it handles 500k+ row files. Clicking a column header sorts ascending or descending with numeric awareness. A live filter searches across all columns, cleared with Escape. The delimiter (comma, tab, semicolon, or pipe) can be auto-detected, and several encodings are supported (UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, Windows-1252, Latin-1). The table follows the system light or dark appearance. A companion app holds settings for delimiter detection and a max-row limit (default 100,000), with a truncation notice when a file exceeds it.
use_cases: preview CSV files in Finder without opening Excel
quickly inspect large CSV or TSV exports
sort and search a CSV file before opening it in a spreadsheet
view semicolon or pipe-delimited data files
check CSV encoding and contents from Quick Look
how_to_run: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Extensions → Quick Look → enable CSV Quick Look
git clone the repository and cd csv-quick-look (optional: change bundleIdPrefix in project.yml)
In Xcode, select the CSVQuickLook scheme and My Mac, then press ⌘R to install the extension
notable: Virtual-scroll table that only renders visible rows, aimed at very large files
Auto-detects delimiter and multiple text encodings including UTF-16 and Windows-1252
Frontend JS/CSS can be edited and reloaded without rebuilding the Swift target
Fully sandboxed with no network access, per the README
caveats: Requires macOS 12 or later; building from source requires Xcode 15 or later
Previews are capped at a configurable row limit (default 100,000), with a truncation notice beyond it
Enabling the extension requires a manual step in System Settings (or System Preferences on macOS 12–13)
keywords: alternative to plain text quick look
